items.title: 68146_Russell Procope oral history interview
items.q: The interviewee discusses Billie Holiday's professional conflict with John Hammond and Count Basie, stating 'I know, because I've been through that situation many times' regarding the pressure to sing blues, but does not claim a personal or professional relationship with Holiday herself.

ctx.x: at Jim and Andy's, he was a little high and he was talking on about that. And a few months later I was doing some research and I came across an old DownBeat from the '30s, and sure enough there was the whole story. She wanted to do, "I Can't Get Started," and he wanted her to do the blues, and she said, "I'm not a blues singer," and he said, "You're not Basie's singer either," and fired her.

Well, I suppose in that case, you see, and again this brings up the subject of, well, now, how can I put it? It brings up the subject of doing what you're told to do. Now, like I say, Fletcher Henderson's band were independent and outspoken, and Billie Holiday was independent and outspoken. Now, John Hammond, he thought that because she was a black singer she had to sing the blues. He wasn't ready to accept her as a singer. He thought Billie Holiday, the blues, that's it. And of course at that time Billie was in…

items.title: 68146_Russell Procope oral history interview
items.q: So I don't blame Billie Holliday one bit.

ctx.x: Well, did you ever hear that John Hammond fired Billie from the Basie band because she wouldn't sing the blues?
